prompt: A director wants a shot that reads a character's emotional reaction clearly while still keeping the audience aware of the room around them. Which shot is the best choice?
teacher_notes: Warm-up item for a shot-size vocabulary unit.
explanation: A medium close-up frames roughly from the chest up, so facial expression reads clearly while part of the background stays visible. An extreme close-up strips away the setting, an extreme wide shot loses facial detail, and an over-the-shoulder two-shot emphasizes the relationship between two characters rather than one character's reaction.
